guide.summary: Production app for outside merchants (app review, wait 7 weeks to 4+ months (reported, not guaranteed)); Sandbox only, prototype (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).
guide.verdict: Sandbox testing is immediate; production needs account verification plus app review with no published timeline, and developers report waits of 7 weeks to over 4 months.

composio.note: Clover is listed under 'Bring your own OAuth app'. Create the auth config with your Clover App ID and App Secret.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed OAuth app for Clover, so you must register your own Clover app and give Composio its App ID and App Secret.
reasons: Composio does not supply a managed app for Clover
Managed apps would show Composio branding on consent screens
Your own app gets dedicated quota and your own scopes

scenarios.label: Production app for outside merchants
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent connects real Clover merchants in production, with the app listed on the Clover App Market.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured: identity documents, app setup, demo video, submission.

waiting.basis: Clover publishes no timeline (c14); developers report 7 weeks and over 4 months (c15, c16).

scenarios.approval: Clover must first verify and approve the production developer account, then review every submitted app.

modifiers.note: Sanctions check repeats monthly after account approval.

extras: Sanctions check repeats monthly after account approval.

scenarios.label: Sandbox only, prototype
scenarios.when_this_applies: You only build and test in the Clover sandbox with test merchants.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured.

waiting.basis: Account approval is not needed for sandbox-only use (c5).

scenarios.approval: No account or app approval is needed in the sandbox.

prerequisites.title: Owner role on a global developer account
prerequisites.detail: Only an owner can accept the Clover Developer Agreement and edit developer settings.

prerequisites.title: Identity and business documents
prerequisites.detail: Individuals need ID and proof of address; companies also need proof of business address and an EIN or Tax ID. Documents are requested by email and due within 10 business days.

prerequisites.title: Required legal links
prerequisites.detail: Provide a privacy policy and terms of service or end user license agreement; Clover checks them against its legal guidelines.

steps.title: Create global developer account
steps.detail: Sign up, and make sure the person has the owner role to accept the Developer Agreement.

steps.title: Create app in sandbox
steps.detail: Create the app in the sandbox Developer Dashboard; App ID and App Secret are assigned automatically.
steps.done_when: App Settings page shows App ID and Secret

steps.title: Configure REST settings and permissions
steps.detail: Draft the Site URL, Default OAuth Response set to Code, and the permission list with reasons. Use v2 OAuth with expiring tokens.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your App ID and Secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and check it is a subpath of the Site URL with matching domain and scheme.

steps.title: Submit production developer account
steps.detail: Switch to production, enter identity and corporate details, and upload requested documents promptly.

steps.title: Wait for account verification
steps.detail: Clover verifies identity and runs a sanctions check; no timeline is published.

steps.title: Prepare demo video and listing
steps.detail: Record a 30 second to 3 minute video of the app workflow and benefit to merchants. Recording is a human task; the agent can draft the description.

steps.title: Submit app for approval
steps.detail: In the production dashboard open Your Apps, click Details, then Submit.

steps.title: Wait for App Market review
steps.detail: Contact Developer Relations if the review runs long.

traps.title: Exceeding the rate limits returns a 429 Too Many
traps.detail: Exceeding the rate limits returns a 429 Too Many Requests error. The page does not tie this to app approval status.

traps.title: Review has no published timeline
traps.detail: Developers report 7 weeks to over 4 months with little communication. Do not plan a launch date around it.

traps.title: Use OAuth tokens, not merchant API tokens
traps.detail: The sandbox allows merchant API tokens, but review requires OAuth tokens for REST API apps.

traps.title: Permission changes force reinstall
traps.detail: Merchants must uninstall and reinstall the app for updated permissions to take effect.

traps.title: Package names cannot be reused
traps.detail: A package name cannot be used across multiple apps, and uploaded APKs cannot be deleted.

blockers.symptom: Verify your Developer Account banner in production
blockers.what_it_means: The production developer account is not yet approved.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit identity and business details and answer document requests within 10 business days.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the document list and draft the application details.

blockers.what_it_means: Clover may not give a reason up front.
blockers.what_to_do: Reply to the rejection email thread to prompt a reason.

open_questions: Rate limits for unapproved versus approved apps were not found. Check Clover's rate-limit page or ask Developer Relations.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: You need an approved developer account to submit an app for approval through the production environment on the Global Developer Dashboard.
evidence.answer: For apps on the Clover App Market, submitting an app for approval through the production environment requires an approved developer account.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Your app is linked to your approved production developer account.
evidence.answer: The app is linked to the developer's approved production developer account.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Clover must verify and approve your production developer account before starting the process of approving your app.
evidence.answer: For Clover App Market submissions, Clover must verify and approve the developer's production developer account before it starts approving the app.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All apps submitted to the Clover App Market are reviewed to make sure they perform as expected, are free of bugs, and add value for merchants.
evidence.answer: For Clover App Market submissions, every submitted app is reviewed by Clover (the review applies to all apps, not only some triggers).

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: All apps submitted to the Clover App Market are reviewed to make sure they perform as expected, are free of bugs, and add value for merchants.
evidence.answer: The Clover App Market review checks that the app performs as expected, is free of bugs, and adds value for merchants.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: The team reviews the functional video and description you provide.
evidence.answer: The developer must upload a functional video and a description of the app's functional workflow, which the team reviews.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: You must upload a video that provides a detailed functional description explaining the workflow of your app to enable quick review and approval of your app.
evidence.answer: The functional video must give a detailed functional description of the app's workflow to enable quick review and approval.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: The video should help the Clover App Market team visualize your app's functional flow and how it benefits the merchant.
evidence.answer: The functional video should show the reviewers the app's functional flow and how it benefits the merchant.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Click the Sandbox toggle icon to go to the production environment.
evidence.answer: On the Clover Global Developer Dashboard, the developer switches to the production environment using the Sandbox toggle icon before working on the app for submission.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: When you create an app, you must select a subscription country because Clover must know the subscription country where your app is available for processing payments.
evidence.answer: When creating an app in the production environment, the developer must select the subscription country where the app is available for processing payments.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Once your app is submitted, the Approval Status in the My Apps section and all other pages for your app display a Pending status.
evidence.answer: After submission, the app's approval status shows Pending while it awaits approval.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Create a production developer account as described in Developer account approval .
evidence.answer: Creating the app requires a production developer account, which must first be approved as described in the Developer account approval section.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: External POS apps using the REST Pay API are not available on the public Clover App market, but your Clover apps are visible to merchants using your integrated POS.
evidence.answer: External POS apps using the REST Pay API are not listed on the public Clover App market, but they are visible to merchants using the developer's integrated POS.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: To complete a payment on the Clover device, you must authorize your app to read merchant data from a Clover device.
evidence.answer: For card-present transactions on a Clover device, the app must be authorized to read Merchant data.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Select the READ checkbox for Merchant.
evidence.answer: The Merchant READ permission is selected on the Edit Requested Permissions page, with a reason entered for the card-present REST Pay case.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If your app lets merchants create and use ECOMM_COMPAT card tokens for card-not-present (CNP) transactions, you must also configure your app for the Ecommerce API.
evidence.answer: Apps that let merchants create and use ECOMM_COMPAT card tokens for card-not-present transactions must also be configured for the Ecommerce API (this step is optional and applies only in that case).

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: In the Ecommerce section, select the Enable online payments checkbox.
evidence.answer: For card-not-present support, the developer selects the Enable online payments checkbox in the Ecommerce section of Requested Permissions.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Optionally, if you are integrating with Cloud Pay Display, enter a domain link (URL) in the CORS Domain field.
evidence.answer: The CORS Domain field is optional and is only needed when integrating with Cloud Pay Display; it takes a domain link (URL).

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Log in to Developer Dashboard .
evidence.answer: Setup starts by logging in to the Developer Dashboard.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Click Create App . The Create App window appears.
evidence.answer: To create an app, click Create App in the Developer Dashboard to open the Create App window.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Select one or more countries where you want to make your app available for Clover merchants.
evidence.answer: During app creation, the developer enters an app name and selects one or more countries where the app will be available to Clover merchants.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Click Create . The App name - App Settings page appears.
evidence.answer: Clicking Create finishes app creation and opens the App Settings page.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: For - Is this app an integration of an existing point of sale? option - select Yes .
evidence.answer: To mark the app as an integration of an existing point of sale, select Web under REST Clients on the App Type page, then choose Yes for the existing point-of-sale question and save.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The App Settings—App Type section displays a Remote App ID (RAID) that uniquely identifies your semi-integrated app.
evidence.answer: After saving the app type, the App Settings page shows a Remote App ID (RAID) that uniquely identifies the semi-integrated app.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: In the Site URL field, enter the link (URL) of the home page of your web app.
evidence.answer: In REST Configuration, the developer enters the URL of the home page of the web app in the Site URL field.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: In the Default OAuth Response field, select Code .
evidence.answer: In the Default OAuth Response field, the developer selects Code.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: When your merchant is authorized through OAuth 2.0, you receive an authorization code.
evidence.answer: When a merchant authorizes through OAuth 2.0, the developer receives an authorization code, which is needed to request an API token for the app's permissions.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Approved developers can submit apps for the Clover App Market. Your app is linked to your approved production developer account.
evidence.answer: Clover App Market apps are submitted by approved developers, and each app is linked to the developer's approved production developer account.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Create a global developer account
evidence.answer: A global developer account must be created before the app-approval path can start.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: The developer must have an owner role to view and edit account settings in the Developer Settings—Developer Info section.
evidence.answer: The developer must have an owner role to view and edit account settings, and only an owner can accept the Clover Developer Agreement.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Only an owner can accept the Clover Developer Agreement
evidence.answer: Only an owner can accept the Clover Developer Agreement.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Clover must verify and approve your production developer account before starting the app approval process.
evidence.answer: Clover must verify and approve the production developer account before the app approval process starts (the account gate comes first).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Account approval is not needed if you intend to use only the sandbox environment.
evidence.answer: Developer account approval is not required if the developer uses only the sandbox environment.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: You can submit your production developer account for approval while building and testing your app on the sandbox, but it is not required .
evidence.answer: Developers may submit their production account for approval while still building and testing on the sandbox, though this is optional.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: As part of the approval process, Clover verifies the individual and corporate information on the application.
evidence.answer: Clover verifies the identity of the developer (individual or corporate) and the information on the developer application.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: In the Identity Verification section, enter the required information to verify the developer’s identity and contact information as follows:
evidence.answer: Developers must enter identity and contact information for verification, including first and last name, date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format, home address, phone number and email.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Developer’s home address, including street, city, 2-character state code, country, and postal or ZIP code as mentioned on a utility bill, bank statement, or other legal document matching the address of the developer account.
evidence.answer: The home address must match a utility bill, bank statement, or other legal document for the developer account; a P.O. box is valid for an organization but not for its individual representative.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: If the developer’s address is outside the intended market, an unexpired passport is required.
evidence.answer: A government ID is needed: an unexpired passport is required when the developer's address is outside the intended market.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Developers in Canada and the United Kingdom (UK) can provide a current driver’s license instead of a passport.
evidence.answer: Developers in Canada and the United Kingdom can provide a current driver's license instead of a passport.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: A valid, unexpired passport or unexpired driver's license (please ensure it includes your date of birth clearly visible)
evidence.answer: For a valid ID, the document must be an unexpired passport or unexpired driver's license with the date of birth clearly visible.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Proof of home address. This can be a phone or utility bill showing the same name and address as your Clover Developer Application.
evidence.answer: Proof of home address can be a phone or utility bill showing the same name and address as the developer application.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: If you are applying as a company, please scan these additional documents to validate your corporate information:
evidence.answer: Companies must also submit proof of business address and proof of EIN/tax ID as government-issued documents.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Employer identification number (EIN) or tax identifier (Tax ID) from a government tax authority-issued document. Length: 9 alphanumeric characters
evidence.answer: Business accounts require an EIN or Tax ID of 9 alphanumeric characters from a government tax authority-issued document.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: If the Clover App Market business team needs to contact you for more information, they will email you with instructions for uploading the required documentation to a secure Clover Box.
evidence.answer: Documents are uploaded by email to a secure Clover Box folder when the Clover business team requests them.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Please provide all documents required for verification within 10 business days of receiving this email or your application may be rejected.
evidence.answer: Required verification documents must be provided within 10 business days of receiving the request email, or the application may be rejected.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: If you do not have a verified developer account, a Verify your Developer Account banner displays on the Production environment.
evidence.answer: Until the production developer account is approved, the developer can only use the sandbox environment; the Verify your Developer Account banner appears on Production if the account is not verified.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Clover must run an Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) check on every developer as part of the approval process.
evidence.answer: Clover must run an OFAC sanctions check on every developer as part of approval, and repeats it monthly after approval.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: After your account is approved, Clover repeats the OFAC check monthly.
evidence.answer: The OFAC check is repeated monthly after the account is approved.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You agree to the Clover App Market Developer Terms by submitting your details.
evidence.answer: Submitting developer details constitutes agreement to the Clover App Market Developer Terms.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Tax Residency Country : Select the country in which you want a payout.
evidence.answer: The developer's tax residency country determines where payouts are made; Business accounts must give a company legal name, country of business and business address.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: You must have an approved production developer account before Clover can approve your apps.
evidence.answer: This page covers semi-integrated apps for Clover devices; an approved production developer account is required before Clover can approve apps.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Create a separate production developer account for each country or region in which you want to create apps.
evidence.answer: A separate production developer account is needed for each country or region where apps will be created.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: To complete this step, the semi-integration team must be able to verify your identity as an Individual developer or Corporate developer .
evidence.answer: The developer must be verifiable as an Individual developer or a Corporate developer.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Your application is linked to a production developer account, and this account needs to be verified and approved before testing can begin.
evidence.answer: The production developer account must be verified and approved before testing of the app can begin there; testing can continue in the sandbox meanwhile.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: The Clover App Market team reviews and approves each developer account you create in a production environment.
evidence.answer: The Clover App Market team reviews and approves each production developer account before apps can be approved.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: You can launch an integrated app for a merchant after both the app and the associated developer account are approved.
evidence.answer: The developer account must be approved, and then the app itself must be submitted and approved in production, before an integrated app can be launched for a merchant.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Once ready for approval, your application is submitted for approval in the production environment.
evidence.answer: Once the app is ready, it is submitted for approval in the production environment; this submission step applies to all apps, with no stated user or install threshold.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Clover reviews your application and checks for compliance with the following:
evidence.answer: Clover checks the submitted app for compliance with the Clover App Market Terms, App Market Policies, and the Clover Developer Agreement.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Required. Link to your privacy policy and your terms of service or end user license agreement. These documents are verified for compliance with Clover Developer Legal Guidelines .
evidence.answer: The app's privacy policy and terms of service or end user license agreement are required and are verified for compliance with Clover Developer Legal Guidelines.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: App name
evidence.answer: The app's listing details are checked, including app name, tagline, description, icon, EULA, support email, support website, support phone number, two or more app benefits, and one or more screenshots.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Compatibility verification checkpoints
evidence.answer: Clover checks that the app's integration works with the platform: the RAID configuration, OAuth use (REST API only), and record-keeping using an external ID.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your connection logic must correctly pass the RAID generated for the application. A misconfigured or missing RAID will cause your merchants to experience slower transaction processing.
evidence.answer: The connection logic must correctly pass the RAID generated for the application; a misconfigured or missing RAID causes slower transaction processing for merchants.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: All interactions with merchant data sent through the Clover server must be authenticated with an OAuth token (and not a merchant API token as allowed in the sandbox environment).
evidence.answer: For REST API apps, all interactions with merchant data sent through the Clover server must be authenticated with an OAuth token, not a merchant API token as allowed in the sandbox.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: To ensure Clover can help troubleshoot issues once the app is live in production, you must maintain a record of each transaction.
evidence.answer: Each transaction must be recorded using the external ID, which links the developer's system to Clover.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: To assist Clover with the review of your app, we highly recommend recording a video of how your app works and its major features.
evidence.answer: A functional demonstration video of the app's features is highly recommended to assist the review; videos must be 30 seconds to 3 minutes long.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: A video demonstrating how your POS interacts with the Clover device is required for each transaction type.
evidence.answer: A payment flow video is required for each transaction type the integration supports.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Video length: 30 seconds to 3 minutes
evidence.answer: Video length must be between 30 seconds and 3 minutes.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Semi-integrations for the US region must support partial authorizations for the integrated application to be approved.
evidence.answer: For the US region, the integration must support partial authorizations to be approved.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: You can continue to test your app on sandbox until it is ready for production.
